newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends easy, gilts down on profit booking.
newsitem.headline: India call ends easy, gilts down on profit booking.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday at 4.25-4.50 percent, down from opening quotes of 4.75-5.50 percent in liquid conditions, dealers said.
Most of the day's trade was at 4.50-5.00 percent with stray deals at 4.25 percent, they said.
Dealers said fund supply with banks was good and rates would remain easy through the week.
They said a 30-billion-rupee auction of eight year bonds scheduled for next Monday will not push rates up much, given current easy liquidity.
"Call will at most go up to 5.5-.65 percent," said a dealer. "Funds supply is good and central bank intervention in the forex market will pump rupees into banks."
The Reserve Bank of India has bought dollars in forward and spot markets in recent days to try and knock a buoyant rupee down.
Dealers said prices of government securities were down on profit-taking but trade was light as the market consolidated ahead of the new bond auction.

The 10.85 percent 2001 stock fell to 100.75 rupees from its previous close of 100.85 rupees, the 12.14 percent 2000 eased to 104.35 rupees from 104.37 rupees and the 13.50 percent 1998 to 103.63 rupees from 103.65, dealers said.
The 12.59 percent 2004 rose to 106.12 rupees from 106.03.
Yields on August 1997 maturity treasury bills fell to 4.75 percent from 4.95 percent, while July 1998 maturity treasury bills yielded 8.03 percent against 8.10 percent.
